interface.signature: int n, int m, int[][] edges, int s -> int[]

preconditions.expression: 1 <= q <= 10 and 2 <= n <= 1000 and 1 <= m <= n * (n - 1) // 2 and 1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n and 1 <= s <= n for all u, v in edges
preconditions.description: The input constraints are satisfied: number of queries (q), nodes (n), edges (m), and node labels (u, v, s) are within specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in edges)
preconditions.description: All edge endpoints (u, v) are valid node labels between 1 and n.
The number of edges provided matches the declared count m.

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == n - 1 and all(0 <= i < n - 1 for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: The returned array has exactly n-1 elements, corresponding to distances for nodes 2 through n (inclusive).

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == -1 or return_value[i] >= 6 for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: Each distance in the output is either -1 (unreachable) or a positive multiple of 6 (edge weight).

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == -1 or return_value[i] == 6 * shortest_path_length for i in range(n - 1))
postconditions.description: For each node j = i + 2 (where i ranges from 0 to n-2), return_value[i] is the shortest path distance from s to j using BFS, multiplied by 6. If no path exists, return_value[i] is -1.

postconditions.expression: all(return_value[i] == -1 or (return_value[i] == 6 * d and d == min_distance(s, j, edges)) for i in range(n - 1) for j in [i + 2])
postconditions.description: The distance for node j (where j = i + 2) is the minimum number of edges from s to j multiplied by 6, or -1 if j is unreachable from s. The shortest path is determined by BFS.
